answer.label: Unconfirmed Coolidge anecdote
answer.sourceLine: This is the punchline of a story in which Coolidge reports a sermon about sin. Wikiquote flags it as apocryphal, citing Nigel Rees; contemporary circulation does not establish that the conversation happened.

author.name: Calvin Coolidge
author.heading: About Calvin Coolidge
author.bio: Calvin Coolidge was a U.S. president known for terse speech. That reputation made him an easy subject for short comic anecdotes.

cite.sourceCitation: Rees, Nigel. Sayings of the Century, p. 67, as cited by Wikiquote; compare Barry Popik, American Dialect Society post, July 16, 2004, transcribing a 1925 newspaper anecdote.
cite.pageCitation: Quotle.info. “Who really said ‘He was against it’?” Last verified 9 Nov 2026.

misattribution.heading: Often misattributed
misattribution.intro: A newspaper printing the anecdote establishes that the story circulated, not that Coolidge actually said its punchline.

sourcesVerified.claim: Wikiquote’s misattribution section gives Rees’s caution. Barry Popik’s fetched American Dialect Society post separately transcribes a December 7, 1925 New York Times report of the anecdote, proving circulation, not the underlying conversation.
